Regulation: B.C. Reg. 162/2026
Made under: Trade Recognition Act
Published in: No. 16 – B.C. Regs. 153 to 162, September 22, including September 8, 2026
Deposit date: September 22, 2026

B.C. Reg. 162/2026, deposited September 22, 2026, under theTRADE RECOGNITION ACT[section 15]. Order in Council 409/2026, approved and ordered September 21, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that, effective October 1, 2026, theTrade Recognition Act, S.B.C. 2026, c. 3, is brought into force. — A. DIX,Minister of Jobs and Economic Growth; K. GREENE,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. minutes_briefs.title: BC's new Trade Recognition Act takes effect October 1, 2026, changing how out-of-province credentials are recognized
minutes_briefs.summary: BC's Trade Recognition Act (a new provincial law about recognizing skills and credentials people earned outside the province) was officially brought into force on October 1, 2026. The law was created by B.C. Reg. 162/2026, an order approved by the Lieutenant Governor in Council on September 21, 2026 and filed on September 22, 2026. The Act is meant to make it easier for workers trained in other provinces or countries to have their qualifications recognized in BC. The regulation itself does not spell out the detailed rules — those come from the Act and any rules made under it.
minutes_briefs.action_required: Check whether your business relies on out-of-province or foreign-trained workers, and review how the new Trade Recognition Act affects how you assess their credentials.
minutes_briefs.industries: Construction & Development, Professional Services, Labour & Employment
